description: An introduction to the six articles of faith in Islam: belief in Allah, His angels, His revealed books, His messengers, the Last Day, and divine decree (Qadar).

mcq.questionText: How many pillars (articles) of Iman are there in Islam?
mcq.explanation: The pillars of Iman are six: belief in Allah, His angels, His books, His messengers, the Last Day, and Qadar.

mcq.questionText: The first pillar of Iman is belief in:
mcq.explanation: Belief in Allah, the One and only God who has no partner, is the foundation and first pillar of Iman.

mcq.questionText: Belief in the Oneness of Allah is known by which term?
mcq.explanation: Tawhid means affirming the absolute Oneness of Allah, while shirk (associating partners with Allah) is its opposite.

mcq.questionText: From what did Allah create the angels?
mcq.explanation: Angels were created from light, jinn from smokeless fire, and human beings from clay.

mcq.questionText: Which angel is responsible for delivering revelation to the prophets?
mcq.explanation: Jibril (Gabriel) is the angel who brought the revelation from Allah to the prophets, including the Qur'an to Prophet Muhammad.

mcq.questionText: The holy book revealed to Prophet Musa (Moses) is the:
mcq.explanation: The Tawrat (Torah) was revealed to Prophet Musa, the Injil to Prophet Isa, the Zabur to Prophet Dawud, and the Qur'an to Prophet Muhammad.

mcq.questionText: The holy book revealed to Prophet Dawud (David) is the:
mcq.explanation: The Zabur (Psalms) was the scripture revealed to Prophet Dawud (David).

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is the final book revealed by Allah?
mcq.explanation: The Qur'an is the last and final revelation, sent to Prophet Muhammad as guidance for all of mankind until the Last Day.

mcq.questionText: Who is the last and final messenger of Allah?
mcq.explanation: Prophet Muhammad is the Seal of the Prophets (Khatam an-Nabiyyin); no prophet will come after him.

mcq.questionText: Belief in the Last Day means believing in:
mcq.explanation: Belief in the Last Day includes belief in the resurrection of the dead, the Day of Judgement, and the reward of Paradise or punishment of Hell.

mcq.questionText: The Arabic term Qadar refers to belief in:
mcq.explanation: Qadar is belief in Allah's divine decree and predestination, that nothing happens except by His knowledge and will.

mcq.questionText: Associating partners with Allah is called:
mcq.explanation: Shirk is the act of associating partners with Allah and is the gravest sin in Islam, the opposite of Tawhid.

mcq.questionText: Which angel will blow the trumpet to signal the coming of the Last Day?
mcq.explanation: Angel Israfil is charged with blowing the trumpet (sur) to mark the end of the world and the resurrection.

mcq.questionText: What is the correct order of the first three pillars of Iman?
mcq.explanation: The pillars in order are: belief in Allah, His angels, His books, His messengers, the Last Day, and Qadar.

mcq.questionText: Belief in the messengers of Allah includes believing that they were:

options.text: Human beings chosen to convey Allah's message

mcq.explanation: The messengers were chosen human beings sent by Allah to guide people; they are not to be worshipped.

fib.questionText: The pillars of Iman are _____ in number.
fib.explanation: The six articles of faith are belief in Allah, angels, books, messengers, the Last Day, and Qadar.

fib.questionText: Belief in the Oneness of Allah is called _____.
fib.explanation: Tawhid affirms that Allah is one, with no partner or equal.

fib.questionText: The angel who delivered revelation to the prophets is _____.
fib.explanation: Jibril (Gabriel) brought Allah's words to the prophets, including the Qur'an.

fib.questionText: The holy book revealed to Prophet Muhammad is the _____.
fib.explanation: The Qur'an is the final revelation and a guidance for all mankind.

fib.questionText: The scripture revealed to Prophet Isa (Jesus) is the _____.
fib.explanation: The Injil (Gospel) was the book given to Prophet Isa.

fib.questionText: Angels were created by Allah from _____.
fib.explanation: Angels are made of light (nur), unlike humans made of clay and jinn made of fire.

fib.questionText: Belief in Allah's divine decree and predestination is called _____.
fib.explanation: Qadar means accepting that everything happens by Allah's knowledge and will.

fib.questionText: Prophet Muhammad is described as the _____ of the Prophets, meaning the last one.
fib.explanation: He is the Seal of the Prophets (Khatam an-Nabiyyin); no prophet comes after him.

fib.questionText: The Day on which all people will be raised and judged is called the _____ Day.
fib.explanation: Belief in the Last Day includes resurrection, judgement, and reward or punishment.

fib.questionText: The opposite of Tawhid, associating partners with Allah, is called _____.
fib.explanation: Shirk is the most serious sin in Islam and contradicts belief in Allah's Oneness.

tf.questionText: There are six pillars of Iman.
tf.explanation: The six are belief in Allah, angels, books, messengers, the Last Day, and Qadar.

tf.questionText: Belief in Allah is the first pillar of Iman.
tf.explanation: Faith in Allah, the One God, is the foundation of all the other articles of faith.
Angels were created from light; humans were created from clay.

tf.questionText: The Qur'an is the final book revealed by Allah.
tf.explanation: The Qur'an was revealed to Prophet Muhammad and is the last divine revelation.

tf.questionText: Muslims believe that the prophets were divine beings who should be worshipped.
tf.explanation: Prophets were human messengers chosen by Allah; worship belongs to Allah alone.

tf.questionText: Belief in the Last Day includes belief in Paradise and Hell.
tf.explanation: After resurrection and judgement, the righteous enter Paradise and the wrongdoers face Hell.

tf.questionText: Qadar means belief in Allah's divine decree and predestination.
tf.explanation: Qadar is the sixth pillar: nothing occurs except by Allah's knowledge and will.

tf.questionText: The Zabur was revealed to Prophet Musa (Moses).
tf.explanation: The Zabur was revealed to Prophet Dawud; the Tawrat was revealed to Prophet Musa.

tf.questionText: Shirk means associating partners with Allah.
tf.explanation: Shirk is the opposite of Tawhid and is considered the greatest sin in Islam.

tf.questionText: Believing in some of Allah's messengers but rejecting others is acceptable in Islam.
tf.explanation: A Muslim must believe in all of Allah's messengers without distinction; rejecting any of them breaks this pillar of faith.

summary.correctAnswer: Belief in Allah, His angels, His books, His messengers, the Last Day, and Qadar.
summary.explanation: These six articles form the core beliefs every Muslim must hold.

summary.correctAnswer: Iman means faith or belief in the heart, confirmed by the tongue and actions.
summary.explanation: True Iman combines inner conviction with outward affirmation and deeds.

summary.correctAnswer: Believing Allah is one, with no partner, the Creator and Sustainer of all things.
summary.explanation: Tawhid is the foundation of faith and the first pillar of Iman.

summary.correctAnswer: Angels are obedient creatures made of light who carry out Allah's commands.
summary.explanation: Examples include Jibril, Mikail, and Israfil, each with assigned duties.

summary.correctAnswer: Allah revealed scriptures including the Tawrat, Zabur, Injil, and the Qur'an.
summary.explanation: The Qur'an is the final and complete revelation for all mankind.

summary.correctAnswer: Allah sent human messengers to guide people, ending with Prophet Muhammad.
summary.explanation: Muslims believe in all prophets without distinction.

summary.correctAnswer: Believing in resurrection, judgement, and the reward of Paradise or Hell.
summary.explanation: This belief encourages good deeds and accountability for one's actions.

summary.correctAnswer: Accepting that everything happens by Allah's knowledge, will, and decree.
summary.explanation: Qadar teaches patience in hardship and gratitude in ease.

summary.questionText: Significance of the pillars of Iman
summary.correctAnswer: They give a Muslim a clear belief system and guide their behaviour.
summary.explanation: Holding all six firmly is what makes a person a believer (mu'min).

summary.correctAnswer: Shirk, which is associating partners with Allah.
summary.explanation: Shirk is the gravest sin and contradicts the first pillar of Iman.

hoq.questionText: Which statement best explains why belief in the Last Day is important for a Muslim's daily conduct?

options.text: It removes all responsibility for one's actions
It encourages accountability, since every deed will be judged
It applies only to the prophets, not ordinary people
It means good and bad deeds have no consequences

hoq.explanation: Belief in resurrection and judgement motivates a believer to do good and avoid wrong, knowing they are accountable to Allah.

hoq.questionText: How does belief in Qadar help a believer who faces a sudden misfortune?

options.text: It leads them to blame the angels for the event
It encourages patience and trust, knowing it occurred by Allah's will
It means they should stop working and making any effort
It proves that Allah has no knowledge of the future

hoq.explanation: Belief in Qadar teaches a believer to remain patient and trust Allah's wisdom, while still taking reasonable action.

hoq.questionText: Why must a Muslim believe in all of Allah's messengers and books rather than only some?

options.text: Because they all came from the same one God with a unified message of guidance
Because each prophet founded a separate religion to compete with the others
Because the earlier books are more important than the Qur'an
Because belief is optional and a matter of personal choice

hoq.explanation: All the prophets and scriptures came from the same God to call people to worship Him alone, so accepting one means accepting the chain of guidance.
